main_text.p: formam addiderunt ; in terminis juris gentium remanserunt. Hypotheca enim & Constitutum tantum jure prætorio ad obligandum facta sunt efficacia. Et circa Emphyteusin, atque Donationes, neque Zenon, neque Justinianus, jura nova introduxerunt; quod isti contractus gentibus non essent incogniti, licet nonnulli forte iisdem proprium nomen imposuerint. Coraf. 1. Mistel. 21. Conuan. 7. comm. c. 12. Hænon. disp. Inst. 1. thef. 14. Henric. Ernst. Cathol. jur. c. 10. n. 7. & 8. diss. Zoef. ex parte. D. just. & jur. n. 44.
main_text.head: CAPUT III.
main_text.p: 1. Quid sit jus Civile in genere, describitur.
3. Quot modis aliquid dicatur juris civilis? Et an stipulatio? Acceptilatio?
5. Unde dignoscatur aliquid esse juris civilis?

1. HActenus egi de jure naturali & gentium, deque iis quæ utrique aut alterutri adscribuntur; superest jus civile, sic acceptum, ut & jus prætorium sub se contineat; ad distinctionem juris naturalis atque gentium. §. 1. Inst. de jur. nat. Gent. & civil. l. 9. D. de Just.

page.notes: The initial "H" of the paragraph is a large woodcut-style letter; the word after it reads as printed. The "Actenus" spelling is partly obscured by the initial. Ornamental marks and dots on the scan are not printed text. The citation lines at the end of the first paragraph are set in the text flow, not in a margin, so they are kept in the main text.
